vulnerabilities.description: Database credentials should not be hardcoded in source code as they can be easily exposed.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use environment variables or a secure configuration management system for database credentials.

vulnerabilities.description: API keys should be stored in environment variables or secure configuration management systems, not hardcoded in source code.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Move API keys to environment variables or use a secrets management service.

vulnerabilities.description: JWT secrets should be stored securely and not hardcoded in source code.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use environment variables or a secure key management service for JWT secrets.

vulnerabilities.description: Email addresses should not be hardcoded in source code as they can be used for phishing attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use configuration files or environment variables for email addresses.

vulnerabilities.description: Phone numbers should not be hardcoded in source code as they can be used for social engineering attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use configuration files or environment variables for phone numbers.

vulnerabilities.description: Social Security Numbers should never be hardcoded in source code as they are highly sensitive PII.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove hardcoded SSNs and use secure data storage with proper encryption.

vulnerabilities.message: Logging SSN during patient object creation
vulnerabilities.description: Logging SSNs violates HIPAA requirements and can lead to data breaches.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove SSN logging entirely or use proper data masking.

vulnerabilities.description: Logging SSNs violates HIPAA requirements and can lead to data breaches.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove SSN logging or implement proper data masking.

vulnerabilities.description: Logging patient DOB can violate HIPAA requirements if not properly secured.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove DOB logging or implement proper data masking.

vulnerabilities.description: Logging patient phone numbers can violate HIPAA requirements if not properly secured.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove phone number logging or implement proper data masking.

vulnerabilities.message: Writing patient data to unencrypted file
vulnerabilities.description: Writing PHI to unencrypted files violates HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Encrypt all files containing PHI or use a secure database with encryption at rest.

vulnerabilities.message: Returning full patient data including SSN and PHI without access controls
vulnerabilities.description: Exposing full patient data without proper access controls violates HIPAA requirements.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement proper access controls and data masking for sensitive PHI.

vulnerabilities.message: Potential SQL injection vulnerability in query construction
vulnerabilities.description: String concatenation in SQL queries can lead to SQL injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements to prevent SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.match: String query = "SELECT * FROM patients WHERE first_name = '" + name + "' OR last_name = '" + name + "'";

vulnerabilities.description: Logging medical history violates HIPAA requirements and can lead to data breaches.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove medical data logging or implement proper data masking.
vulnerabilities.match: logger.info("Updated medical history for patient " + patientId + ": " + medicalHistory)

vulnerabilities.description: Logging patient diagnosis violates HIPAA requirements and can lead to data breaches.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Remove diagnosis logging or implement proper data masking.
vulnerabilities.match: logger.info("Updated diagnosis for patient " + patientId + ": " + diagnosis)

vulnerabilities.message: Exposing SSN in API response without masking
vulnerabilities.description: SSNs should be masked or excluded from API responses to prevent data exposure.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Mask SSNs (e.g., ***-**-6789) or exclude them from responses unless absolutely necessary.

vulnerabilities.message: Exposing PHI data in API response without proper controls
vulnerabilities.description: PHI data should be protected and only exposed to authorized users with proper access controls.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement proper access controls and data masking for all PHI data.

vulnerabilities.message: Using weak encryption algorithm (MD5) for sensitive data
vulnerabilities.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken and should not be used for any security purposes.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use SHA-256 or better for hashing, and AES-256-GCM for encryption.

complianceViolations: HIPAA Privacy Rule - Uses and disclosures
CCPA Section 1798.100 - General duties of businesses

recommendations: Immediately remove all hardcoded credentials and secrets
Implement proper secrets management using environment variables or a vault service
Remove all PHI logging and implement HIPAA-compliant audit logging
Implement proper encryption for all PHI data storage and transmission
Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
Implement proper access controls and role-based permissions for PHI
Use modern encryption algorithms (AES-256-GCM) instead of MD5
Implement proper data masking for all PHI in API responses
Conduct a comprehensive HIPAA compliance audit
Implement proper audit trails for all PHI access and modifications
Use secure file storage with encryption at rest for all PHI data
Implement proper error handling that doesn't expose sensitive information
